proposal_corrections: The proposal said Xenophon's Socrates leads Euthydemus to piety as 'knowledge of how the gods ought to be honoured'. At IV.6.4 the definition accepted is knowing what is lawful (τὰ νόμιμα) concerning the gods; 'how one must honour' is the step at IV.6.3. The app quotes Dakyns's wording of 6.4.

The proposal's medieval prompts (Ibn Sina, Metaphysics of the Healing I.6; Aquinas ST I q2 a3; Maimonides, Guide I.58) and the Kant–Wollstonecraft pairing were held back: no public-domain English Ibn Sina to check against; Aquinas, Maimonides and Kant's 1784 essay are not bundled and the reading route does not need them now. Wollstonecraft is bundled, as the proposal said.

The proposal's Presocratic prompt kept its river question; Plato's Cratylus 402a and Parmenides fr. 8 are not bundled, so the passage is anchored in Aristotle, Met. IV.5 (bundled, next on the route), with B12 quoted in Graham's translation.
